LESSON: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 2.1: Independent reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Independent reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what you read b) locate information from print  Learners find answers to questions through on your own?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read
2. read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDEPENDENT READING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Independent reading helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: INDEPENDENT READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Independent reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading

What this means
In this part you learn to read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Independent reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Independent reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Independent reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Independent reading to a partner. (skill: read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Independent reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read.
3. Practise this skill: read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Independent reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Independent reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Independent reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what you read b) locate information from print  Learners find answers to questions through on your own?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Independent reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main idea in a  Learners make and confirm predictions from you understand 5 lessons passage texts read what you read.
5. Be able to: read supplementary books with available in the library for independent understanding reading.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
